clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient is a 71‑year‑old male with advanced CKD (eGFR 7.3) that dominates his clinical picture. Recent NSTEMI with elevated high‑sensitivity troponin suggests myocardial injury, most likely type 2 MI driven by supply‑demand mismatch in the setting of CKD, possible anemia, and uncontrolled hypertension. The combination of prior MI, CKD, and possible volume overload raises the likelihood of acute decompensated HFrEF (cardiorenal syndrome). Additional common contributors—primary hypothyroidism, statin‑related liver injury, and benign hyperbilirubinemia (Gilbert syndrome)—explain the persistent hypercholesterolemia, marked bilirubin elevation, and cytopenias. Gaps such as missing blood pressure, BMI, smoking status, bilirubin fractions, and medication adherence limit certainty, prompting targeted work‑up.

recommended_workup: Serial high‑sensitivity troponin measurements (0 h, 3 h) and 12‑lead ECG to differentiate type 2 MI from plaque‑rupture NSTEMI
Transthoracic echocardiogram plus BNP/NT‑proBNP to assess ejection fraction and volume status
Fractionated bilirubin (direct vs indirect), ALP, GGT to characterize hyperbilirubinemia
Thyroid panel (TSH, free T4) to evaluate for primary hypothyroidism
Comprehensive medication reconciliation with pharmacy fill data; consider holding one statin pending liver re‑evaluation
Liver ultrasound (or MRCP if direct bilirubin predominates) to rule out obstructive biliary disease or assess for NAFLD
Hemolysis work‑up: LDH, haptoglobin, reticulocyte count, peripheral smear, direct Coombs test
Full vital signs assessment: clinic BP, home BP logs, weight trend, physical exam for JVP/edema
Repeat CBC after temporary discontinuation of suspect drugs to see if leukopenia/thrombocytopenia improve
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio and repeat eGFR to monitor CKD progression
Psychosocial screening (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) and referral to social services for housing support
STOP‑BANG questionnaire and overnight oximetry if sleep apnea is suspected
